meta.face: Twin Roman brothers of about thirty-five with fair olive complexions and ONE SHARED bone structure, told apart only by the beard: a face with a BROAD, SQUARE forehead above a NARROWER, V-SHAPED lower face ending in a POINTED chin — a LONG nose with a distinct BUMP at the bridge, LARGE, dark eyes set CLOSE together under THICK, STRAIGHT black brows that nearly meet, clearly PROMINENT ears, a small, full mouth; short, crisp, curly black hair. MARCUS (left) wears a short, close black beard; MARCELLIANUS (right) is clean-shaven, which shows the pointed chin; both gazes grave and steadfast.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The book tells twin brothers of an illustrious Roman family, married, imprisoned under Diocletian, strengthened by St. Sebastian, and at last pierced with lances; its engraving shows two young, beardless men bound to pillars. Wikipedia: nothing certain is known but their names, their martyrdom and their burial on the Via Ardeatina in the cemetery of Balbina; the twins, parents and Sebastian come from the largely legendary Acts of St. Sebastian. The shared face is our choice.
